title: Subcellular localisation of newly synthesized viral RNA in coronavirus infection by EM autoradiography
author: Ronald W.A.L. Limpens
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfrtjm6n
materials: Prepare the solutions for development of the samples. The gold solution and the fixative can be stored (at 4 °C and Room temperature , respectively) for successive development sessions. Solutions A & B need to be freshly prepared every time. Development starts 1h after the last chemical of solution B has dissolved. It is convenient to prepare solutions A & B in T175 cell culture flasks, because these are clean and phosphate free. Gold-solution: 2% HAuCl 4 in autoclaved milliQ water Gold latensification (Solution A): 1 mL 2% H-AuCl 4 in 100 mL autoclaved milliQ water Add 250 mg potassium thiocyanate + 300 mg KBr Add autoclaved milliQ water to 500 mL Elon-Ascorbic acid (Solution B): 225 mg elon (metol) and wait until it dissolves Add 1500 mg ascorbic acid and wait until it dissolves Add 1300 mg anhydrous borax (or 2500 mg borax decahydrate) and wait until it dissolves Add 500 mg KBr and wait until it dissolves Add autoclaved milliQ water up to 500 mL Fixative (Solution C): 24% sodium thiosulphate in milliQ water
Transfer the glassware, solutions and the box containing the samples to the darkroom.
Inside the darkroom, fill Coplin jars with solutions A, B and C, and have some extra containers for milliQ water.

steps.title: Infect Cells
steps.instruction: Infect cells with virus, preferably at a high multiplicity of infection (MOI ≥5).

substeps.instruction: Include a control sample without radioactive label (skip step 3).
Include a mock-infected control sample (replace virus inoculum with mock-inoculum).

steps.title: Block Cellular Transcription
steps.instruction: One hour before applying the radioactive label, replace the normal culture medium with culture medium containing 10 µg/ml actinomycin D.

steps.title: Apply Radioactive Label
steps.instruction: Remove the medium and quickly add the radioactive label ([5- 3 H]-uridine, 500 µCi/ml) in medium containing 10 µg/ml actinomycin D.

steps.title: Fix Cells
steps.instruction: After the desired labelling time (20-60 min), remove the label and chemically fix the cells.

substeps.instruction: Fix with 1.5% glutaraldehyde in 1 M cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4) for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Keep samples in the fixative overnight at 4°C.

steps.title: Wash Samples
steps.instruction: Wash extensively with 0.1 M cacodylate buffer to remove unincorporated radioactive label.

steps.title: Prepare EM Grids
steps.instruction: Cut 50 nm sections of the sample and place them on EM grids, preparing 10 grids per sample.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Post stain grids with 7% uranyl acetate and Reynold’s lead citrate for additional contrast.

steps.title: Mount Grids on Glass Slides
steps.instruction: Attach grids to cleaned, dry glass slides using double-sided sticky tape.

substeps.instruction: Clean microscope glass slides with ethanol and let dry.
Apply a strip of double-sided sticky tape along the long side of the slide.
Press grid edges against the tape, ensuring each slide includes a grid for every condition tested and appropriate controls.

steps.title: Apply Carbon Layer
steps.instruction: Evaporate a thin layer of carbon (around 10 nm) on each glass slide to prevent chemographic effects.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclear Emulsion
steps.instruction: Prepare the photographic emulsion in a dark room using an Ilford 902 or 904 safelight filter.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 mL of Ilford L4 nuclear emulsion to 25 mL of milliQ water in a glass cylinder.
Heat the emulsion to 42 °C while stirring in a water bath for 30 minutes.
Cool the emulsion to roughly 20 °C until it forms a thin, clear membrane in a wire loop.

steps.title: Apply Emulsion to Slides
steps.instruction: Apply the emulsion layer to the glass slides and allow to dry.

substeps.instruction: Press the emulsion loop parallel onto the samples so the layer attaches to the grids.
Lay slides on a flat surface for 10 minutes to dry.

steps.title: Store and Expose Samples
steps.instruction: Store slides in a light-tight plastic box with silica gel at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Seal the box with dark tape (avoid cardboard or wooden boxes).
Regularly evaluate exposure progress via EM until sufficient autoradiography grains are present (this may take weeks to several months).

steps.title: Develop the Emulsion
steps.instruction: Develop the slides at a constant temperature of approximately 20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Clean all glassware with 30% acetic acid for 10 minutes, rinse several times with milliQ water, and dry.
Remove one slide from the box and close the box immediately.
Place the glass slide in solution A for 5 minutes.
Rinse briefly in milliQ water.
Rinse briefly in 2% acetic acid.
Rinse 3 times for 1 minute each in milliQ water.

steps.title: Recover and Analyze Grids
steps.instruction: Remove grids from the slide immediately after the final rinse and dry on filter paper.

substeps.instruction: Store dry grids in a gridbox and transfer outside the darkroom.
Inspect samples in the electron microscope to assess signal strength.
If signal is insufficient, wait 1-3 weeks before developing another slide; if sufficient, develop remaining slides.

steps.title: Final EM Processing
steps.instruction: Process samples for EM using chemical fixation or high-pressure freezing and freeze-substitution, following standard protocols for epoxy resin embedding.
